question.knowledge_point: Integrating a Rational Functions With a Repeated Factor of Degree Higher Than Two
question.worked_solution:
First, we must convert the integrand into a sum of partial fractions:

$$
\frac{3x+1}{(x+1)^{3}}=\frac{A}{x+1}+\frac{B}{(x+1)^{2}}+\frac{C}{(x+1)^{3}}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B,$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $(x+1)^{3}$ and get

$$
3x+1=A(x+1)^{2}+B(x+1)+C.
$$

Plugging in $x=-1,$ we can eliminate $A$ and $B$ and solve for $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3(-1)+1 & =A(-1+1)^{2}+B(-1+1)+C \\ -2 & =C\end{aligned}
$$

Now, plugging in $x=0$ and substituting the known value of $C,$ we get an equation relating $A$ and $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3(0)+1 & =A(0+1)^{2}+B(0+1)+C \\ 1 & =A+B-2 \\ A+B & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, plugging in $x=-2$ and substituting the known value of $C,$ we get an equation relating $A$ and $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3(-2)+1 & =A(-2+1)^{2}+B(-2+1)+C \\ -5 & =A-B-2 \\ A-B & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the equations $A-B=-3$ and $A+B=3,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2A & =-3+3 \\ 2A & =0 \\ A & =0,\end{aligned}
$$

and substituting back into $A+B=3,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}0+B & =3 \\ B & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integrand as the partial sum

$$
\frac{3x+1}{(x+1)^{3}}=\frac{3}{(x+1)^{2}}-\frac{2}{(x+1)^{3}}.
$$

Finally, we integrate this expression term by term to get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3x+1}{(x+1)^{3}}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{3}{(x+1)^{2}}-\frac{2}{(x+1)^{3}})\,\text{d}x \\  & =3\int \frac{1}{(x+1)^{2}}\,\text{d}x-2\int \frac{1}{(x+1)^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{3}{x+1}+\frac{1}{(x+1)^{2}}+K,\end{aligned}
$$

where $K$ is an integral constant.
